title: Handwriting Legibility Scoring
subtitle: PyTorch CNN Fine-Tuning

demoInstructions.lead: Draw a digit (0-9) or load a sample, then score how legible it is.
bullets: Pick a sample from “Daniel’s Handwritten Numbers”, or draw a digit on the canvas.
Use the eraser to clear the canvas and try another digit.
Review the predicted digit, confidence, and legibility score breakdown.

problem: My wife says my handwriting is hard to read. I wanted an objective score.
actions: Built three digit-recognition models, moving from a simple baseline to a CNN.
Trained on MNIST (60,000 digits) and selected the best model.
Deployed it behind a serverless scoring API for the live demo.
results: The best model reached ~99% test accuracy on MNIST (see notebook).
On a small personal handwriting set, accuracy was ~75.6% (not a benchmark; see notebook).

evaluation.goal: Recognize handwritten digits and use model confidence as one input to a legibility score.
evaluation.dataset: MNIST plus a small personal handwriting set used only as a domain-shift check.
evaluation.split: Standard MNIST training and test datasets: 60,000 training digits and 10,000 test digits.
evaluation.baseline: The first model reached 92.302% accuracy on the MNIST test set.

metrics.label: Best MNIST test accuracy
metrics.context: Model v3, selected from the three notebook architectures.

metrics.label: Personal handwriting accuracy
metrics.context: Small custom set; included as a domain-shift check, not a benchmark.

evaluation.decision: Selected model v3 because it produced the highest recorded MNIST test accuracy.
limitations: MNIST is a narrow digit-recognition dataset and does not represent general handwriting legibility.
The custom handwriting sample is small and its size is not documented in the published result.

notes: MNIST is the training baseline; the personal handwriting scores are a domain-shift check, not a full handwriting benchmark.
